# Executive Summary

This document analyzes sectoral payroll expenditure and wage growth dynamics across the Danish economy using real-time administrative data retrieved from **Danmarks Statistik** via API. By integrating industry-level hourly earnings data (Table `LONS40`) with total employment statistics (Table `RAS300`), the analysis models aggregate annual payroll spend from 2013 to 2024 across primary, secondary, and tertiary economic sectors.

```{r danish-payroll-pipeline, echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, fig.width = 14, fig.height = 8}
# Load Libraries
library(danstat)
library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)

# --- DATA PULL: Table LONS40 (Hourly Wages) ---------------------------
wage_data <- get_data(
  table_id = "LONS40",
  variables = list(
    list(code = "BRANCHE07", values = NA),
    list(code = "SEKTOR", values = "1000"),
    list(code = "AFLOEN", values = "TIFA"),
    list(code = "LONGRP", values = "LTOT"),
    list(code = "LØNMÅL", values = "FORINKL"),
    list(code = "KØN", values = "MOK"),
    list(code = "Tid", values = NA)
  )
)

wage_clean <- wage_data %>% 
  subset(select = c(BRANCHE07, TID, INDHOLD)) %>% 
  rename(
    hourly_wage = INDHOLD,
    industry = BRANCHE07,
    year = TID
  ) 

# --- DATA PULL: Table RAS300 (Employment Numbers) --------------------
employed_data <- get_data(
  table_id = "RAS300",
  variables = list(
    list(code = "BRANCHE07", values = NA),
    list(code = "Tid", values = NA)
  )
)

employed_clean <- employed_data %>%
  filter(TID >= 2013) %>% 
  rename(
     num_employees = INDHOLD,
     industry = BRANCHE07,
     year = TID
  ) 

# --- DATA TRANSFORMATION & CALCULATIONS -------------------------------
payroll <- inner_join(wage_clean, employed_clean, by = c("industry", "year")) %>%
  mutate(
    hourly_wage = as.numeric(hourly_wage) / 100, # Scaled to convert into true DKK/hr
    num_employees = as.numeric(num_employees),
    total_payroll_dkk = hourly_wage * num_employees * 1600 # 1,600 standard working hours/year
  )

payroll_summary <- payroll %>%
  arrange(industry, year) %>%
  group_by(industry) %>%
  mutate(
    log_payroll = log(total_payroll_dkk),
    pct_growth = (total_payroll_dkk - lag(total_payroll_dkk)) / lag(total_payroll_dkk) * 100
  )

# --- SUMMARY TABLES ---------------------------------------------------
top_spenders <- payroll_summary %>%
  filter(!industry %in% c("TOT Industry, total", "TOT", "10000", "000000", "I alt")) %>%
  filter(year == max(year)) %>%
  arrange(desc(total_payroll_dkk)) %>%
  head(5)

fastest_growing <- payroll_summary %>%
  filter(!industry %in% c("TOT Industry, total", "TOT", "10000", "000000", "I alt")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(pct_growth)) %>%
  group_by(industry) %>%
  summarise(avg_annual_growth = mean(pct_growth)) %>%
  arrange(desc(avg_annual_growth)) %>%
  head(5)

kable(top_spenders, caption = "Top 5 Sectors by Total Payroll Spend (DKK)")
kable(fastest_growing, caption = "Top 5 Sectors by Average Annual Growth Rate (%)")

# --- VISUALIZATION ----------------------------------------------------
payroll_summary %>% 
  filter(!industry %in% c("TOT Industry, total", "TOT", "10000", "000000", "I alt")) %>% 
  mutate(year = as.numeric(as.character(year))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = as.numeric(year), y = total_payroll_dkk / 1e9, color = industry)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = c(seq(2013, 2023, by = 2), 2024),
    limits = c(2013, 2024)
    ) + # Clean whole-year ticks
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_dollar(prefix = "DKK ", suffix = "B")) +
  labs(
    title = "Annual Payroll Expenditure by Industry (Denmark)",
    subtitle = "Excludes macro total to highlight sector-level dynamics",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Total Payroll (Billions DKK)",
    color = "Industry Code"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
